and it does help to have a sparkplug socket

It is highly recommended because most people don't under stand the ability of touque to disalign the socket angle resulting in busted sparkplug porceline (the white part lol).

The spark plugs and socket has two things that are handy. First and most important is the rubber insert that helps not break the plug and also holds the plug in the socket so you don't drop it. (((PROTIP: use an old spark plug wire Boot with the wire removed as spark plug installing starter tool. It quickly gets the plug threaded with zero risk of cross threading and it give a handy handle to your plug for screwing in with two fingers. If you have a deep recess spark plug hole then super glue a spark plug boot to your old srewdriver and you just made a long installer tool. Don't forget.. don't over tighten. A little goes a long way on spark plugs. )))

Top tip,if access is hard due to a recessed type plug hole use 3/8 hose slipped over the ceramic end...in the case of cross threading the rubber hose will slip unlike a socket and save the threads in the head.....a simple job but can turn into disaster if you damage the plug threads in the cyl head even experianced techs can have a mishap this trick has saved me a few times

I'd also say to invest in a few 1inch extensions. You can slip the socket in the recessed hole, then add some 1" extensions until you have the correct length. This is great when you need an extension, but only have a few inches of clearance.
Also helps to use an appropriate plug socket with a rubber ring inside a lot of people try a deep socket but this can go bad quockly if it slips

Yes, I have had to re-tap threads in a head and also do a helicoil repair. This is a bitch and you do NOT want to do that unless you don't have much else to do on Saturday. Be careful with those threads!

Spend the extra few dollars for platinum plugs, fewer changes, better performance and mileage. Do it yourselfers should get a spark plug gap tool, or feeler gauges to confirm the gap, don't assume they are gapped correctly by the factory.

Examine the old plugs as they are removed, there should be a light grey deposit on them. Black deposits indicate an oil ring issue.
